page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 219.0 GB of system memory, yielding 54.69 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB SSD, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark data indicates that the M8-4ms exhibits limited processing and memory throughput capabilities relative to other server classes. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1035.08 falls in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 2724.76 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 151.25 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 17.19 GB/sec. Similarly, Geekbench scores are low, with a single-core score of 885.0 and a multi-core score of 1970.0, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested systems.

The primary tradeoff of the M8-4ms is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio contrasted against its low computational and memory bandwidth performance. While it provides a dense 219.0 GB memory footprint, the underlying Intel Xeon processor and memory subsystem deliver weak throughput, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 1023.36 and a Redis SET operations rate of 2.63 million operations per second. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server is positioned for workloads requiring massive memory capacity rather than raw compute power or high-speed data processing.

This instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high CPU performance. Suitable applications include large in-memory caching layers, legacy enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM footprints, and basic database operations that fit entirely within the 219.0 GB memory space. It is not suited for compute-heavy tasks, software compilation, or real-time large language model inference.
